subject: Re: ACME - Reranking model validation & A/B plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Rerank validation next steps + recommended models

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion on your ranking objectives and the production constraints (median latencies < 120ms P95, 4M qps traffic pattern spikes). Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Summary of fit: based on the examples you shared and the initial eval set, we think a small-to-medium reranker with quantization-friendly weights (candidate: rwd-rerank-v2-quant) plus prefix-KV caching looks like the best balance of latency and NDCG lift.

2) Benchmarks we ran on your holdout (private dataset): preliminary metrics attached + on Drive — NDCG@10 delta vs baseline: +0.042, MRR: +0.031. (see sheet: ndcg_mrr_results_v1.xlsx)

3) Prompt/feature set: attached is the prompt_sets_v1 we used (short description in header). Please review — we tried to preserve your entity normalization and session features.

4) Risks / quality regression concerns: the biggest risk is title-heavy queries where the model reweights lexical signal too strongly. We recommend keeping a small lexical-weighted baseline for fallback. Also, we flagged a ~1.5% drop on a small subset of ASIN-only queries — we can run targeted evals if you want.

5) Proposed A/B plan: 2-week A/B, 50/50 split, evaluate NDCG@10 and MRR weekly, safety/fallthrough monitoring, automated rollback if NDCG delta < +0.02 or error rate increases >0.2%.

Next steps / asks for you:
- Confirm you'd like us to run the A/B (we can host test traffic on a Dedicated pool or provide config for your side).
- Share any additional redline queries or privacy constraints.
- We can set up a short weekly status cadence for the 2-week test.

Links / artifacts: Drive folder with raw evals and prompt sets: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleLink
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/contact/ACME-42

Attachments: acme_prompt_sets_v1.csv, ndcg_mrr_results_v1.xlsx, proposed_ab_plan.pdf

Thanks — I’ll queue Rishi to share more on the evaluation methodology and the exact NDCG/MRR breakouts.

—Marissa

On Fri, Jul 2, 2026 at 10:03 AM Samir Patel <samir@acme.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A couple quick clarifying questions before we greenlight the A/B:
>
> 1) Can you confirm the test traffic approach? We prefer Redwood-hosted test (dedicated pool) but need an estimate on the additional cost and isolation details.
> 2) For the ASIN-only regressions you flagged: can you share the sample queries and the magnitude of the drop (absolute % on that slice)?
> 3) Any compliance or retention impacts if we host the evals on Redwood Dedicated (we have to keep some logs for 90 days for fraud detection, but will need SOC2 evidence).

Hi Samir — quick notes from the eval/ops side: 

1) Test traffic approach/cost: Redwood-hosted Dedicated pool is straightforward — we can spin up a reserved worker pool for the 2-week test. Estimated incremental cost for a medium pool handling your 10k qps baseline with 2x burst headroom is ~$12k for 2 weeks (we can provide a firm quote from SalesOps). Data isolation: logs/eval artifacts will be stored in a customer-scoped bucket tied to your account; we support KMS keys if you want customer-managed keys.

2) ASIN-only regression details: the flagged slice contains ~1.2% of total eval queries. Absolute performance drop on that slice: NDCG@10 dropped from 0.642 -> 0.628 (delta -0.014); MRR dropped -0.011. We included 25 example queries in the Drive folder under /regressions/sample_asin_examples.txt. The regression is concentrated in very short, SKU-only queries where the reranker overvalues title token overlap. Mitigation: add a lexical boost for SKU matches or keep the lexical baseline for those queries.

3) Compliance/retention: hosting on Dedicated preserves SOC2 scope — we can share SOC2 Type II report and provide audit logs. For the 90-day retention you mentioned, we can set retention policy to 90 days and if needed redact user identifiers in the eval set (we recommend hashed IDs).

Attached: ndcg_mrr_results_v1.xlsx (breakouts by query cohort), proposed_ab_plan.pdf (traffic split, rollback criteria, monitoring dashboard metrics). Below is the core eval summary table (quick copy):

- Holdout size: 150k queries (stratified by doc type)
- Baseline (lexical-only) NDCG@10: 0.612
- rwd-rerank-v2-quant NDCG@10: 0.654 (delta +0.042)
- Baseline MRR: 0.573
- rwd-rerank-v2-quant MRR: 0.604 (delta +0.031)
- Latency median (in our infra sim): 72ms; P95: 118ms (with small KV cache warmup)

Proposed A/B specifics:
- Duration: 2 weeks
- Traffic split: 50/50 (control = current lexical baseline, treatment = rwd-rerank-v2-quant)
- Metrics: primary = NDCG@10 (cohort-weighted), secondary = MRR, latency P95, error rate, and a manual regression check on SKU-only slice.
- Rollback: automatic if treatment NDCG delta < +0.02 at 95% CI or error rate increases >0.2%; manual rollback if critical regressions in SKU-only slice (>1% absolute drop on that slice).

If that looks good I can schedule the Dedicated test capacity and send a short runbook for monitoring.

—Rishi
